test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A trader borrowed some money from a trader against which Rs. 8,000 is due in one year. The trader wants to settle the account after 2 months. If the rate of interest is 9% per annum, how much will he have to pay (rounded off)?
solution:
**Given:** 

Final amount is due in one year = 8000 Rs

Rate of interest = 9 % per annum

trader wants to settle the account after 2 months.

**Formula used:**

**large {P. W.} = {Final \:amount times 100over {100 + ({Rtimes {Mover 12}})}}**

Where P.W. is the present worth, Final Amount is the actual amount, R is the rate of interest percent and M is the time (in years).

The trader wants to settle the account after 2 months, and given the amount is due 1 year

Therefore M = 12 – 2 = 10..

**Calculation:**

=> large {P. W.} = {8000 times 100over {100 + ({9times {10over 12}})}}

=> large {P. W.} = {8000 times 100over {100 + ({ 7.5})}}

=> large {P. W.} = {8000 times 100over {107.5 }}

=> P.W. = 7441.86

**Hence, he will have to pay 'Rs. 7442'.**
